jobs.occupation: Post-Doc position: AI-Driven Robotic Experimentation for Controlling Metal Degradation (Chemiker/in)
jobs.description: Metal degradation can be a boon or a bane, depending on the application and on how well we can control it. A corroding car component is a safety risk. A biodegradable metal implant that dissolves at exactly the right rate spares patients a second surgery. An aqueous battery lives or dies depending on what happens at its electrodes.At the Department of Electrochemistry and Big Data we unravel degradation pathways of light metals used in structural applications, medical devices and aqueous batteries. For these applications, degradation can be controlled using tailored electrolyte additives. The chemical space of possible additives is virtually infinite, so we do not test one-by-one. We run a robotic, high-throughput testing platform coupled with machine learning and AI agents that help to decide which experiment to run next. Join us to build the self-driving laboratory of corrosion science.We are offering a 2‑year Post-Doctoral position, as soon as possible, in the quickly developing field of robotic experimentation in materials science. The position is full-time (39 h/week) and will be located in Hereon's main campus, in Geesthacht (near Hamburg).We value diversity and welcome applications from people of all backgrounds. We particularly encourage qualified women to apply.Your tasks- Run and extend automated experimental workflows on our robotic platform to test how light alloys respond to electrolytes of increasing complexity- Discover high-performing organic and inorganic compounds that control degradation for structural and biomedical applications- Work side by side with computational scientists to build structure-property models, and use AI agents to accelerate screening- Uncover the mechanisms behind effective degradation control, and turn them into design rules for pre-selecting promising compounds- Publish your results in leading journals, present at international conferences, write project reports and contribute to open, FAIR datasetsYour profile- A completed master's and PhD degree in chemistry, electrochemistry, materials science, computational materials science or a related field- Solid experimental skills in chemical laboratories and confidence in quantitative data analysis using appropriate software- Experience with corrosion, electrochemical methods or light alloys (Mg, Al, Zn)- Experience with lab automation, electronic lab notebooks, FAIR data, databases or machine learning- Curiosity about automation and AI, and motivation to work at the interface of experiment and computation- Very good English, knowledge of the German language is preferred but not mandatory, we support language learningContent-related enquiries regarding this position can be directed to Sviatlana.Lamaka(at)hereon.de.Our offer- Access to state-of-the-art (robotic) labs, unique scientific and technical infrastructure- Access to a large international research and industrial network.- Funding for conferences, summer schools and courses needed or research stays- An exciting and varied job in a research center with around 1,000 employees from more than 60 nations- An International Welcome Office with guest accommodation- 6 weeks holiday per year; company holidays between Christmas and New Year's DaySocial benefits under the collective agreement for the German public sector and remuneration up to pay grade 13 (EntgO Bund)A well-connected research campus, good networking opportunities, a subsidized Deutschlandticket (job ticket) subject to certain conditions, and charging facilities for electric vehicles- Individual opportunities for further training- An excellent technical infrastructure and modern workplace equipment- A family-friendly working environment with childcare options, e. g. a daycare center close to the workplace- Workplace health promotion programmes, e.g. an Employee Assistance Program (EAP)- Corporate Benefits- A varied canteen offering on campusSchwerbehinderte und diesen gleichgestellte behinderte Personen werden bei gleicher Qualifikation und Eignung im Rahmen der gesetzlichen Bestimmungen bevorzugt berücksichtigt.Bitte bewerben Sie sich mit Ihrem vollständigen Bewerbungsprofil (Lebenslauf, Motivationsschreiben, sonstige Referenzen) über unsere Karriereseite.

The University Hospital Essen offers first class medical services in the Ruhr metropolis. Every year, 225.000 patients are treated in 30 clinics, 27 institutes and specialized centers. The over 8.000 employees offer medical care with state-of-the-art diagnosis and therapies, which meet highest international standards. Patient care is connected with basic and translational research at an internationally competitive level.Hemoglobin is best known for its role in oxygen transport in red blood cells. Our preliminary findings indicate that it is also expressed by lung immune cells, where it may contribute to antiviral defense. These findings further suggest that the thrombospondin-1 (TSP-1)/CD47 signaling axis limits hemoglobin expression and its associated antiviral antivity.The project aims to uncover the molecular mechanisms underlying hemoglobin-mediated antiviral defense and determine how this response is regulated by TSP-1/CD47 signaling. Combining mechanistic studies with in vivo models, we will explore whether targeting this pathway can enhance antiviral immunity while avoiding excessive inflammation and lung tissue damage.At the Insitute of Medical Microbiology (working group of PD Dr. Torben Knuschke), we are therefore offering the following position, which is fully funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) and will start on 1 January 2027Perform in vitro and in vivo experiments to characterize the intrinsic and extrinsic (paracrine) funtions of hemoglobin in lung immune and epithelial cellsApply molecular biology techniquesPlan, perform, and analyze therapeutic intervention studiesPresent research findings at national and international conferences and contribute to peer-reviewed publicationsAssist in supervising Bachelors/Masters studentsA completed Master´s degree (or equivalent) in Biology, Molecular Medicine, Immunology, Biochemistry, or a related fieldSolid background in cell culture and standard molecular biology techniquesExperience in laboratory animal science (FELASA B) is an advantageStrong interest in basic research in Virology/ImmunologyIndependent, structured, and team-oriented working-styleExcellent written and spoken English skills; German language skills are a plus but not requiredAn exciting, methodologically diverse PhD project in an internationally visible research fieldDedicated supervision of the doctoral project within a cooperative working group with regular seminarsState-of-the-art laboratory infrastructure at University Hospital EssenInterdisciplinary work with colleagues from other departmentsEnrollment into the Graduate School for Biomedical Sciences BIOME (https://www.uni-due.de/biome)Salary according to the German public sector pay scale (TV-L, E13, 65%), fixed-term for 3 yearsA collegial working environment that encourages independent scientific ideasFamily-friendly corporate culture

Your area of responsibility Research topic: Plant immunity Plant pathogens secrete small molecules in their host to manipulate cellular processes and cause disease. Plants are not defenseless, however, and have evolved a wide variety of immune receptors to sense these pathogen-associated molecules and subsequently trigger an immune response to restrict pathogen infection. In the Molecular Plant Immunity research group, we investigate the molecular basis of effector recognition and immune receptor activation, and how evolutionary forces shape these processes. We then leverage this knowledge to develop strategies for sustainable disease resistance in crops. Your tasks:• Independent execution of molecular biology laboratory tasks• Microbiological work with bacteria and fungi under sterile conditions• Organization and maintenance of standardized workflows in the laboratory• Plant husbandry• Support lab members in their experiments• Documenting experimental procedures and resultsYour profile• Completed training as a Biological technical assistant or equivalent• Independent and solution-oriented work ethic• Enthusiasm for teamwork• Ability to work in a multi-cultural, multi-ethnic environment with sensitivity and respect for diversity• Desirable knowledge and skills include:• Good English language skills (written and spoken)• Experience in microbiology and molecular biology work• Experience in handling biosafety S1 organismsPlease apply with a cover letter and your CV containing the contact details of two referees and by the 7th of December 2026. If you have any questions, please contact Clemence Marchal (clemence.marchal@ipb-halle.de).We offer• Modern Working Conditions: Comprehensive introduction to work techniques and a modern research environment with state-of-the-art equipment and up-to-date software• Career Development: Targeted training opportunities and access to a specialized library with electronic resources and quiet workspaces• Compensation & Security: Classification according to TV-L including annual bonus, pension scheme (VBL), health offers, and discounted canteen meals• Ideal Working Environment: A varied and inspiring workplace in an international setting at a leading scientific and innovation hub• Team Spirit and Leadership Culture: An open culture that strengthens teamwork, enables career networking, and promotes your research skills.• Work-Life Balance: Flexible working models, remote work options, and 30 days of annual leave – for a balanced work-life experience.About us The Leibniz Institute of Plant Biochemistry (IPB) is a non-university research institution of the Leibniz Association on the Weinberg Campus of the Martin Luther University Halle-Wittenberg. As a foundation under public law, the IPB is under direct supervision of the state of Saxony-Anhalt.The IPB is an internationally recognized research institution and consists of four scientific Departments, additional independent junior research groups, and the Department Administration & Infrastructure (about 200 employees, including about 40 PhD students). Research at the IPB aims to understand the (bio)chemical basis of plant resilience and performance in challenging environments related to climate change. The IPB offers excellent research facilities and state-of-the-art infrastructure to investigate the chemical diversity, biochemical interactions, and biological roles of small natural molecules in plants and fungi, with an emphasis on specialized metabolites, chemical mediators, and relevant molecular networks of functional gene and protein regulation (https://www.ipb-halle.de/en/).Dr. Clemence MarchalResearch AssociateTelefon: 0345 55821440clemence.marchal@ipb-halle.deLeibniz-Institut für Pflanzenbiochemie (IPB)Weinberg 306120 Halle (Saale)

jobs.occupation: GlobalFoundries Management Services GmbH & Co. KG: Expansion Project Coordinator - Global Supply Man (Ingenieur/in - Mikroelektronik)
jobs.employer_name: GlobalFoundries Management Services GmbH & Co. KG
jobs.description: About GF  GlobalFoundries® Inc. (GF®) is one of the world's leading semiconductor manufacturers. GF redefines innovation and semiconductor manufacturing by developing and delivering feature-rich process technology solutions with leading performance in all growth markets. GF offers a unique mix of design, development and manufacturing services. With a talented and diverse team and manufacturing locations in the U.S., Europe and Asia, GF is a trusted technology provider to its global customers. GF employs approximately 15,000 people, including more than 3,000 in Dresden, Germany.For more information, visit hier .Introduction  As Expansion Project Coordinator, you will hold a strategic procurement role focused on securing a competitive supply of manufacturing equipment and services for GlobalFoundries’ Dresden operations. You will collaborate closely with Operations to define requirements and with the broader Global Supply Management team to leverage the global supply base, commercial expertise, technical knowledge, and best practices. A key focus of this position is equipment-related capital expenditure (CAPEX), particularly the coordination and execution of our fab expansion sourcing activities to support timely, competitive, and well-aligned procurement decisions. Your Job  - Coordinate procurement workstreams across the Equipment Commodity team and fab-expansion stakeholders, including Finance, Planning, Engineering and Facility. - Develop and execute sourcing strategies for CAPEX equipment and services in alignment with expansion milestones, budgets, and global commodity objectives. - Serve as the primary commercial interface with equipment suppliers, driving capacity commitments, delivery schedules, technical alignment, and supplier development. - Lead local commercial negotiations and support global negotiations for equipment purchases, installation services, warranties, and long-term support agreements. - Use strategic sourcing and analytical tools—including Power BI, cleansheeting, and negotiation planners—to evaluate costs, track commitments, and support investment decisions. - Identify and mitigate commercial, supply, schedule, and capacity risks that could affect fab-expansion milestones. - Resolve project-specific supply issues in collaboration with Operations, Industrial Engineering, and other key stakeholders. - Manage contractual agreements, change orders, claims, and renegotiate project-specific commercial and technical objectives. - Monitor and communicate sourcing progress, savings, risks, supplier commitments, and key decisions to project leadership and relevant stakeholders. - Ensure all procurement activities support applicable Environmental, Health, Safety, Security, and regulatory requirements throughout the expansion project. Required Qualifications- Bachelor's/Master's Degree in Engineering, Science, Business Administration and/or relevant field of study - Minimum of 2 years relevant work experience in an industrial environment - Good command of English and German, both written and verbal (C1)- Good organizational skills and the ability to manage multiple tasks and priorities in a structured manner- Ability and willingness to travel internationally including Singapore and USA from time to time  Preferred Qualifications- Knowledge of materials and/or their application in semiconductor manufacturing, quality requirements and related supply base - Proficiency in sourcing related skills including sourcing strategy development and execution, contract management and supplier performance management - Ability to lead projects and cross-functional teams - Experience in a semiconductor environment or related industryWe Offer  The position is limited for 2 years and to be filled as soon as possible.Attractive compensation components:   13th month salary, bonus payments, assistance with relocation to Dresden.  Flexible working time arrangements:   Family friendly part-time models, trust flextime, salary conversion into free time.Diverse opportunities for further development:   Career stages for every job, internal qualification offers, promotion of external educational qualifications.Focus on your health:   On-site gym and beach volleyball court, bike leasing, subsidized employee restaurant.Corporate culture:   Cooperation at eye level - everyone is on first name terms with us, budget for individual team events, social commitment via GlobalGives.Diversity is part of our corporate DNA. For this reason, we would like to encourage women in particular to apply for a job with us. As we value equal opportunities and inclusion is particularly important to us, we welcome applications from people with disabilities.The job advertisement refers up to pay grade ENG/IC2 at GlobalFoundries ETV.Information about our benefits you can find here: hierSchlagworte: CHIP,Englisch, EmpfehlungsbundQuelle/Bewerbung via: https://www.empfehlungsbund.de/jobs/308354/expansion-project-coordinator-global-supply-management (https://www.empfehlungsbund.de/jobs/308354/expansion-project-coordinator-global-supply-management#apply_form)Kurzinfo zum UnternehmenÜber GFGlobalFoundries (GF) ist ein führender Hersteller von Halbleitern, auf die sich die Welt zum Leben, Arbeiten und Vernetzen verlässt. Wir sind innovativ und arbeiten mit unseren Kunden zusammen, um energieeffizientere und leistungsfähigere Produkte für die Automobilindustrie, intelligente mobile Geräte, das Internet der Dinge (IoT), Kommunikationsinfrastrukturen und andere wachstumsstarke Märkte zu entwickeln.Mit unserem globalen Produktionsnetzwerk, das sich über die USA, Europa und Asien erstreckt, sind wir eine vertrauenswürdige und zuverlässige Quelle für Kunden in aller Welt. Jeden Tag liefert unser talentiertes und vielfältiges Team Ergebnisse mit einem unnachgiebigen Fokus auf Sicherheit, Langlebigkeit und Nachhaltigkeit. GF beschäftigt weltweit rund 13.000 Mitarbeitende, davon 3.000 in Dresden. Weitere Informationen finden Sie unter www.gf.com.
